recommendation.summary: S6 transactional patch set of 5 function(s) (interface-level (signature/added/removed functions) with call-graph closure change).
justification: no state-schema, dependency, toolchain, goroutine-structure or long-running-code change
every member of the patch set is an ordinary non-generic function or method, so each can be redirected through its slot, and the whole set is published in one atomic PatchSet store
signature changes and removals were closed over their callers; new functions and types live in the patch plugin
alternatives: S2 Go plugin swap of the affected handler (same toolchain; old code leaks)
S1 epoch swap if v2 is compiled in alongside v1 (pre-staged release)
S5 FD-passing handoff (identity state transfer) or rolling update as fallback
risks: new package-level variable github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/microservices-demo/src/frontend.frontendMessage: under S6 it lives in the patch plugin and is re-initialised by every later patch generation
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 5 functions
5 patched functions are in package main; a Go plugin cannot import package main, so hotpatchgen must relocate them into an importable package
type information is partial (408/408 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
